name: Second Battle of El Alamein
note: This plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: the formations are corps, groups and divisions, drawn as a schematic of a front about 40 miles long. The Eighth Army stood in the east and faced west; the coast lay to the north and the Qattara Depression to the south. The minefields, the Devil's gardens and the successive lines are not drawn. The accounts do not give an exact position for each division inside its corps, so the corps are drawn as single blocks, the northern one standing for the four infantry divisions of XXX Corps. The Kidney feature, Tel el Aqqaqir, Woodcock and Snipe are placed from their stated distances from each other, the 7th Motor Brigade's two battalions are drawn as one block, and Point 29 near the coast, only roughly. The paths of the moves are drawn straight, and where the accounts say a move was repulsed or left positions unchanged the block is drawn at its furthest point. The Axis infantry line stands for the German and Italian infantry alternating along the front, with the Folgore division drawn apart because the accounts name it in the south. Ariete is counted in the southern armoured group, of which the accounts say one third went north.

phases.title: The armies stand in their lines
phases.text: The Eighth Army stood in the east with XXX Corps in the north, XIII Corps in the south and X Corps ready to exploit. Rommel split his armour into a northern and a southern group, held the 90th Light Division further back and kept the Trieste Division in reserve near the coast.
phases.quote: Rommel held the 90th Light Division further back and kept the 101st Motorised Division

phases.title: The break-in: infantry advance, armour is held up
phases.text: After a barrage, the four infantry divisions of XXX Corps advanced into the Axis minefields and the armour crawled up behind. Only about half of the infantry reached their objectives and none of the tanks broke through. In the south XIII Corps met determined resistance.
phases.quote: Only about half of the infantry attained their objectives and none of the tanks broke through.

phases.title: Axis tanks counter-attack from the Kidney feature
phases.text: At dusk tanks of the 15th Panzer and Littorio Divisions advanced from the Kidney feature against the 1st Armoured Division. Over 100 tanks fought and half were destroyed by dark, with neither position altered.
phases.quote: Over 100 tanks were involved and half were destroyed by dark; neither position was altered.

phases.title: The Australians attack Point 29
phases.text: Montgomery turned XXX Corps north towards the coast with the 9th Australian Division. The 26th Australian Brigade attacked Point 29 at midnight with artillery and 30 tanks, and took the position and 240 prisoners.
phases.quote: The 26th Australian Brigade attacked at midnight, supported by artillery and 30 tanks of the 40th Royal Tank Regiment.

phases.title: Rommel counter-attacks at Point 29
phases.text: Rommel, convinced that the main assault would come in the north, ordered the 15th Panzer and 164th Light Divisions, with part of the Italian XX Corps, to retake Point 29. Under constant artillery and air attack the counter-attack came to nothing.
phases.quote: He ordered a counter-attack against it by the 15th Panzer Division and the 164th Light Division, with part of the Italian XX Corps to begin at 15:00

phases.title: Rommel brings his armour north
phases.text: Rommel reversed his policy of spreading his armour along the front. The 90th Light Division came forward and the 21st Panzer Division went north with a third of the Ariete Division. A shortage of fuel meant the move could not be reversed.
phases.quote: Rommel reversed his policy of distributing his armour across the front

phases.title: A night attack on Woodcock and Snipe
phases.text: The 2nd Battalion, The Rifle Brigade attacked Snipe and the 2nd Battalion, King's Royal Rifle Corps attacked Woodcock. Both had difficulty finding their way in the dark and dust: the KRRC dug in short of its objective, the Rifle Brigade where it judged Snipe lay.
phases.quote: At 23:00 on 26 October 2 Battalion, The Rifle Brigade would attack Snipe and 2nd Battalion King's Royal Rifle Corps (KRRC) would attack Woodcock.

phases.title: Rommel's attacks at Snipe and Point 29 fail
phases.text: At 16:00 German and Italian tanks attacked the Rifle Brigade at Snipe, which held its ground and destroyed 22 German and 10 Italian tanks, and was withdrawn that evening. The 90th Light Division's attack on Point 29 was broken up by artillery and bombing before it reached the Australians.
phases.quote: At 16:00, Rommel launched his major attack. German and Italian tanks moved forward against the Rifle Brigade

phases.title: Operation Supercharge and the charge of the 9th Armoured
phases.text: Two assault brigades cleared a path from 01:05 and gained most of their objectives. At 06:15 the 9th Armoured Brigade advanced on the Axis gun line and failed to create the gap, though it caused great damage.
phases.quote: The brigade had sacrificed itself upon the gun line and caused great damage but had failed to create the gap

phases.title: The Axis tanks counter-attack and fail
phases.text: The remains of the 9th Armoured Brigade came under the 1st Armoured Division, which had deployed. The northern and southern armoured groups counter-attacked at 11:00 and failed under shells and bombs at a cost of about 100 tanks.
phases.quote: At 11:00 on 2 November, the remains of the 15th Panzer Division, 21st Panzer Division and the Littorio Division counter-attacked the 1st Armoured Division

phases.title: The front is broken and Rommel orders a retreat
phases.text: British armour burst a 19-kilometre hole in the Axis front. Rommel could wait no longer for Hitler's reply and at 17:30 gave the order to retreat. The two armoured groups pulled back to the west.
phases.quote: At 17:30, unable to wait any longer for a reply from Hitler, Rommel gave orders to retreat.
